label: Verdict
description: If the composite scores below its best parent, the parent wins. feature.md §0.5 calls this 'arithmetic, not judgment' — so it is arithmetic, and there is no operation here at all: every output is an expression over the scores this state was handed.

inputs.candidates.description: Needed here because the winner is a CANDIDATE and the scores only carry its id.

inputs.mandatory_id.description: The id of the do-nothing / reuse candidate, so its margin can be measured.

outputs.winner.description: The composite only wins when it beats its best parent outright. Ties go to the parent: a composite that merely matches has added complexity for nothing.

outputs.runner_up_margin.description: Winner minus runner-up. A near-tie says the scoring itself found the choice arbitrary, which is what confidence reads it for. With FEWER THAN TWO candidates there is no runner-up: `at(..., -2)` indexes off the end, and the subtraction that used to happen anyway produced NaN — a number that satisfies `{"type":"number"}`, records in the journal as `null`, and cannot be canonicalized. 1 is what `confidence` defaults this slot to, and means the same thing here: no margin pressure, because nothing competed.

outputs.mandatory_margin.description: Winner minus the do-nothing / reuse candidate. Barely beaten is the case where building was probably wrong. Guarded the same way as `runner_up_margin`: the mandatory candidate is supposed to be scored, and `find` returning nothing would subtract `undefined` and yield NaN — the failure this phase actually hit, in its sibling.

outputs.earlier_phase_finding.description: True when the winning candidate is only good because it changes a decision an earlier phase already made. feature.md §0.5 makes that a finding, not a licence.
